title: Cover-local pullback preservation identifies the entire covering nerve
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with all objects, arrows and covering indices in the common universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor. Fix a covering $\mathcal U=\{f_t:U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ of $\mathcal C$. Assume that $u(\mathcal U)=\{u(f_t):u(U_t)\to u(U)\}_{t\in T}$ is a covering of $\mathcal D$ and that for every $t\in T$ and every morphism $a:V\to U$ the canonical map $$u(V\times_U U_t)\longrightarrow u(V)\times_{u(U)}u(U_t)$$ is an isomorphism. No condition is imposed on other source coverings. Choose all tuple fibre products and their index maps for both families as in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. For $n\ge0$ and $\mathbf t=(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\in T^{n+1}$ put $W_{\mathbf t}=U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{t_n}$ and $P_{\mathbf t}=u(U_{t_0})\times_{u(U)}\cdots\times_{u(U)}u(U_{t_n})$. The canonical map $c_{\mathbf t}:u(W_{\mathbf t})\to P_{\mathbf t}$, characterized by $\mathrm{pr}_k c_{\mathbf t}=u(\mathrm{pr}_k)$, is an isomorphism. For every map $\alpha:\{0,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,\ldots,n\}$, write $\mathbf t\alpha=(t_{\alpha(0)},\ldots,t_{\alpha(m)})$, and let $\alpha_W^*:W_{\mathbf t}\to W_{\mathbf t\alpha}$ and $\alpha_P^*:P_{\mathbf t}\to P_{\mathbf t\alpha}$ be the projection-characterized index maps. Then $$c_{\mathbf t\alpha}\circ u(\alpha_W^*)=\alpha_P^*\circ c_{\mathbf t}.$$ No global continuity, final object or preservation of arbitrary pullbacks is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof: the image covering and the displayed iterated fibre-product identity, with its projection-compatible canonical maps made explicit. The assertion isolates the assumptions of continuity for the one fixed covering only (Sites Tag 00WV, definition-continuous).

proof.text: Write $p_k:W_{\mathbf t}\to U_{t_k}$ and $q_k:P_{\mathbf t}\to u(U_{t_k})$ for the chosen projections. Since $u(f_{t_k})u(p_k)=u(f_{t_k}p_k)$ is independent of $k$, the tuple universal property in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex](a) gives a unique $c_{\mathbf t}$ with $q_kc_{\mathbf t}=u(p_k)$. We prove by induction on the positive tuple length that the cone $(u(W_{\mathbf t}),u(p_k))$ itself has this universal property. For length one both chosen objects are $u(U_{t_0})$, their projections are identities and $c_{(t_0)}$ is the identity.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof, displayed iterated fibre-product identity; elementary expansion using Sites Tag 00WV, definition-continuous, condition (2).

proof.text: For the induction step write $\mathbf t=(\mathbf s,j)$, where $\mathbf s$ is nonempty, put $V=W_{\mathbf s}$, and let $a:V\to U$ be its structure map. Let $v:W_{\mathbf t}\to V$ be the prefix index map and $l:W_{\mathbf t}\to U_j$ the last projection. Site axiom (iii) in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) gives $R=V\times_U U_j$ with projections $r_1,r_2$. Its binary universal property means that pairs of maps into $V,U_j$ agreeing over $U$ lift uniquely to $R$. There are inverse maps $h:W_{\mathbf t}\to R$ and $k:R\to W_{\mathbf t}$: $h$ is specified by $(v,l)$, and $k$ by the tuple $(p_i^{\mathbf s}r_1)_i,r_2$. These tuples have equal composites to $U$. The equations $hk=1_R$ and $kh=1_{W_{\mathbf t}}$ follow by composing with $r_1,r_2$ and with every tuple projection respectively; the prefix equality $vk=r_1$ follows by composing with each $p_i^{\mathbf s}$. This is a direct use of (a),(b) of the cited definition.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof, displayed iterated fibre-product identity; elementary expansion using Sites Tag 00WV, definition-continuous, condition (2).

proof.text: Since $u(\mathcal U)$ is a covering, site axiom (iii) in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) also gives $Q=u(V)\times_{u(U)}u(U_j)$ with projections $x,y$ and the binary universal property just stated. The hypothesis for precisely the original member $f_j:U_j\to U$ and the morphism $a:V\to U$ gives an isomorphism $b:u(R)\to Q$ with $xb=u(r_1)$ and $yb=u(r_2)$. Thus $e=b\,u(h):u(W_{\mathbf t})\to Q$ is invertible with inverse $u(k)b^{-1}$: the two composite equations are $b\,u(hk)b^{-1}=1$ and $u(kh)=1$. Moreover $xe=u(v)$ and $ye=u(l)$. Consequently a pair of arrows into $u(V),u(U_j)$ agreeing over $u(U)$ lifts uniquely to $u(W_{\mathbf t})$: lift to $Q$ by its binary instance of (a), then compose with $e^{-1}$. Only this specified base change is used.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof, displayed iterated fibre-product identity; elementary expansion using Sites Tag 00WV, definition-continuous, condition (2).

proof.text: To verify the induction claim, take an arbitrary object $Z$ of $\mathcal D$ and arrows $z_i:Z\to u(U_{s_i})$ and $z_*:Z\to u(U_j)$ having a common composite to $u(U)$. By the induction hypothesis there is a unique $z:Z\to u(V)$ with $u(p_i^{\mathbf s})z=z_i$. Because $\mathbf s$ is nonempty, $u(a)z=u(f_{s_0})z_0=u(f_j)z_*$. Step 3 therefore gives a unique $w:Z\to u(W_{\mathbf t})$ with $u(v)w=z$ and $u(l)w=z_*$. It has every required tuple projection, since $p_i^{\mathbf t}=p_i^{\mathbf s}v$. Conversely, any arrow with those tuple projections has prefix $z$ by the induction hypothesis and last projection $z_*$, hence equals $w$ by Step 3. This proves existence and uniqueness for the longer tuple and completes the induction.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof, displayed iterated fibre-product identity; elementary expansion using Sites Tag 00WV, definition-continuous, condition (2).

proof.text: Both $u(W_{\mathbf t})$ with its mapped projections and $P_{\mathbf t}$ are now tuple fibre products. The unique projection-compatible isomorphism in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex](a) has forward map $c_{\mathbf t}$ by Step 1, so this canonical map is an isomorphism. Equivalently, lift the projections of $P_{\mathbf t}$ into $u(W_{\mathbf t})$ using Step 4; each composite with $c_{\mathbf t}$ is the identity because its projections are those of the identity. This also covers independently chosen, rather than recursively chosen, tuple products.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof, displayed iterated fibre-product identity; elementary expansion using Sites Tag 00WV, definition-continuous, condition (2).

proof.text:
For an arbitrary $\alpha:\{0,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,\ldots,n\}$, compose the two asserted maps with the $k$-th projection $q'_k$ of $P_{\mathbf t\alpha}$. By (b) of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] and functoriality,
$$q'_k c_{\mathbf t\alpha}u(\alpha_W^*)=u(p'_k)u(\alpha_W^*)=u(p'_k\alpha_W^*)=u(p_{\alpha(k)})=q_{\alpha(k)}c_{\mathbf t}=q'_k\alpha_P^*c_{\mathbf t}.$$
The uniqueness part of (a) makes the two maps equal. This includes repetitions and permutations of indices, as well as face and degeneracy maps. If $T$ is empty there are no positive-length tuples and both conclusions are vacuous; no empty product or final object has been used.
